subject: Banking
title: Interest Rate Decisions
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Interest Rate Decisions.

hook.text: Eight times a year, the Fed meets to decide interest rates. Markets move billions on every word of the announcement.

buildup.text: The federal funds rate is the rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed controls this rate directly.

discovery.text: When the Fed changes this rate, every other rate follows: mortgages, car loans, credit cards, and savings accounts.

twist.text: The Fed doesn't set rates by law. It uses open market operations to push the rate where it wants.

climax.text: One number set eight times a year controls the cost of money for the entire economy. That's extraordinary power.

punchline.text: Eight meetings, one rate. It controls the cost of borrowing for everyone.

quiz.question: How often does the Fed meet to set interest rates?
